problems.title: Squeaks
symptoms: My door creaks when I open it

plan.diagnosis: The hinge pin is dry and its metal rubs as the door swings. Lifting the pin out, wiping it and oiling it stops the squeak for a year or more.

steps.check: The door is shut, so it holds itself up while a pin is out.

steps.instruction: Tap the top hinge pin up and out
details: Push up from below with a nail and tap with a hammer.
Do one hinge at a time.
steps.check: The pin is out in your hand.

steps.instruction: Wipe it and coat it with a little oil
details: Petroleum jelly or 3-in-1 oil works; skip WD-40, it dries out.
steps.check: The pin is clean with a thin coat of oil.

steps.instruction: Slide the pin back in and swing the door
details: Repeat on the other hinges if it still squeaks.
steps.check: The door opens without a squeak.

rig_beats.caption: Tap the pin up and out

problems.title: Won't stay closed
symptoms: I have to slam the door to close it

plan.diagnosis: The door has sagged a little, so the latch misses the hole in the metal plate on the frame. Tightening the top hinge screws lifts it back; a long screw in the top hinge fixes it for good.

steps.instruction: Close the door slowly and watch the latch
details: Rub a little lipstick or chalk on the latch to mark where it hits.
steps.check: You can see if the latch hits above or below the hole.

steps.instruction: Tighten the screws in the top hinge
details: Open the door to reach them.
steps.check: All the top hinge screws are tight.

steps.instruction: Still loose? Swap one screw for a 3-inch screw
details: Use the middle hole on the frame side of the top hinge.
steps.check: The long screw bites into the wall framing and pulls the door up.

steps.instruction: Close the door and check it latches
details: If it still misses, the strike plate can be moved up or down a little.
steps.check: The door clicks shut without slamming.

rig_beats.caption: It should go in this hole

problems.title: Sticks or rubs the frame
symptoms: The door rubs on the frame
The door is hard to close

plan.diagnosis: A door that rubs at the top corner on the latch side has sagged from loose hinge screws. Tightening them, or adding a long screw to the top hinge, pulls it back into line.

steps.check: You can see a shiny worn spot or feel where it catches.

details: A screw that spins and won't tighten needs a longer one.
Humid weather swells doors; a little sanding on the rubbing edge helps if needed.
